reason: E1 directly supports that RTA on Si/SiO2 induces high-anisotropy phases via substrate strain and demonstrates a 40-fold coercivity increase in FeCoNiMnCu, but it does not show L10 ordering in a FeCoNi-based alloy without Pt; the claim of L10-like ordering in the base FeCoNi system is an extrapolation not directly evidenced. E2 provides magnetic characterization but does not address ordering or coercivity enhancement.
premises: RTA of transition metal alloy films on Si/SiO2 induces high-anisotropy phase formation via substrate-induced strain
RTA can induce L10-like chemical ordering in FeCoNi-based high-entropy thin films
L10 ordering enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy and coercivity
The baseline FeCoNi-based alloy is a disordered fcc solid solution with low coercivity
The proposed mechanism applies specifically to thin films on rigid substrates
